title: Generalisation, overfitting and early stopping
summary: Population versus empirical risk, bias–variance, independent/group/time splits, checkpoint selection and a complete evidence audit.

objectives.description: Define empirical and population risk and the assumptions supporting a held-out estimate.
Derive bias–variance decomposition with the correct randomness and independence.
Implement explicit early-stopping selection and state restoration.
Audit leakage, paired/clustered uncertainty, baselines and deployment claims.

preparation.description: Read overfitting, validation, memorisation and early stopping; distinguish procedure selection from final evaluation.

activities.title: Lecture notes and primary reading
activities.instructions: Work through the notes with the assigned source open. Reproduce each worked calculation or derivation on paper, including its assumptions, before reading the next step. Write one question that remains unresolved.

activities.title: Problem sheet: calculation, explanation and transfer
activities.instructions: Attempt the problems independently first. Use one hint at a time if useful, and record which help you used. Show the reasoning that connects the model and its assumptions to each answer; compare the reference only after a substantial attempt.

activities.title: Return without the notes
activities.instructions: On a later study day, close the notes and reconstruct the core relation and its assumptions, then explain the failure case from the last problem. Compare with your saved work and correct one gap. This practice does not itself certify mastery.

exitCheck.description: Use the whole problem sheet to judge the objectives: explain assumptions, complete the independent calculations and justify the final transfer/synthesis. The final exercise is the recorded checkpoint; its acceptance alone is not a claim that all course outcomes are mastered.

commonMisconceptions.claim: Any train/validation/test array split guarantees independence.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Groups, near-duplicates, future information and preprocessing can cross the boundaries.

commonMisconceptions.claim: Training loss must rise when overfitting starts.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Training loss can keep falling while validation performance worsens.

commonMisconceptions.claim: Many seeds on one dataset measure all uncertainty.
commonMisconceptions.correction: They describe algorithmic variability conditional on that dataset, not all sampling or distribution-shift uncertainty.
